panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph shows scalp hair with multiple whitish nodules along the hair shafts, matching the captioned white piedra manifestation. No skin is visible for skin tone assessment; age is from the in-text mention of a 45-year-old patient.
panels.attribution_text: Roshan et al. White piedra in a mother and daughter.. International journal of trichology 2009. doi:10.4103/0974-7753.58559. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Whitish to cream-colored easily detachable nodules of size 1-1.5 mm present over the shaft of almost all the scalp hair
in_text_mentions: A 45-year-old lady presented with asymptomatic whitish nodules in the scalp hair for the past 3 years along with breakage of the hair shafts [Figure 1]. Her 20-year-old daughter also had similar complaints for the past 6 months. Both of them had the habit of tying their wet hair up in a knot after a hair wash and shared a common comb. There was no pediculosis in either of them.
